messages.subject: Using WAIC
parts:
I have been using Stan to estimate 2 parameter IRT models with roll call data from the House and Senate.  I recently decided to estimate a common space model by relying on the overlap of legislators that served in both legislatures (so called "bridges").  I also thought why not use House and Senate votes on versions of the same bill as "bridges."  This latter restriction seems intuitive to me but I am wondering if there is a way to test it.  Would estimating the model with and without imposing that the roll call locations are the same and then using WAIC be appropriate in this case? 

Any thoughts are much appreciated.

messages.author: a236d3d356ca53fd
messages.subject: Re: Using WAIC
parts:
WAIC and LOO are appropriate if you want to check the predictive performance for predicting a result of a new vote or results of several votes independently. I recommend using PSIS-LOO instead of WAIC as it is more robust and has more reliable diagnostics, too.

Aki
